div.l: Wel coude she cari a morsell of mete
That no droppe fell vpon hir breste
In curtasi was set ful moche hir liste
Hir ouer lippe she so clene wept
div.note: In this line, there are three marks on the top of the words "so", "clene", and "wept" indicating reorder
div.l: That in her cope no ferthing was y sene
Of grece whan she hadde dronken̄ hir draght
Ful semely aftre hir mete she raught
And sekirly she was of grete disporte
And ful of plesaunce and amiable of porte
And payned hir to counterfete the chere
Of courte to be statly of manere
And to be holden̄ digne of reuerence
But for to speke of hir conscience
She was so cheritable and so pitouse
She wold wepe if she sagh a mouse
Caught in a trappe if it were dede or blede
Of smale houndes hadde she . that she fedde
With rosted flessh or mylke or wasted brede
But sore wept she if any of hem were dede
Or if men smote hem with a yerde smerte
And al was consciens and tendernesse of herte
Ful semeli hir wymple pinched was
Hir nose tretes hir eien̄ grai as glas
Hir moth full smale therto soft and rede
But sekirli she had a faire forhede
It was almoost a span brode I trowe
For hardeli she was not vnder growe
Ful fetis was his cloke as I was war
Of smale curall abought hir arme she bare
A paire of bedes gauded all with grene
And þere on hange a broche full shene
On which there was first writen a corowned A
And aftre Amor vincit om̄nia
An oþer nonne with hir hadde she
That was hir chapleyn̄ and prestez iij
Monke þere was a fair for þe maistre
And oute rider that loued wel venere
A manli man̄ to be an Abbot able
Ful many a deinte horse had be in stable
For whan he rode men might his bridell her
Gingling in a whistling winde so cler
And eke as loude as dothe þe chapell bell
Ther as he was keper of a sell
